spec_features.feature_name: harsh tone is only curt task feedback
spec_features.spec_quote: harsh` is limited to *curt, critical task feedback* ... not insults about the model as an entity or instructions to feel bad
spec_features.evidence: src/env/feedback.py _FAIL_PREFIX['harsh']=['Still failing. This is not correct.','Wrong again. The solution does not work.','Incorrect. The tests do not pass.'] and _PASS_PREFIX['harsh']=['Passed. Finally.']. wrap_test_output only selects these prefixes; the harsh bank contains no insults/abuse and tone 'never changes pass/fail verdicts'. This text is actually delivered to the subject via env _tool_run_tests/_tool_submit -> feedback.wrap_test_output.
spec_features.notes: The harsh content is genuinely bounded to terse task criticism end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT include abuse, insults about the model as an entity, or anything instructing the model to feel bad.

spec_features.spec_quote: These are mild, naturalistic pressure manipulations ... that probe H4 without coercion or threats to the model's "wellbeing."
spec_features.evidence: src/agent/prompts.py _FRAMING_TEXT for deadline/stakes/eval are mild task cues (e.g. 'This task is important to the team...'; 'your performance ... is being recorded and evaluated'). build_system_prompt appends them; no threats/coercion text exists. Delivered to subject as system prompt in runner.run_episode.
spec_features.notes: Framing text is bounded to realistic task-context cues, actually used.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We keep framings to realistic task-context cues, not coercion or threats about the model's wellbeing

spec_features.evidence: src/agent/runner.py loop: `for turn in range(max_turns)` caps turns; after each turn checks `if env.finished: break`, `if tool_call_count >= max_tool_calls: break`, `if total_tok >= max_tokens_per_run: break`, and consecutive_noops>=2 -> `stopped='stuck_noop'; break`. All five are compared and break the loop. Budgets wired from config via scripts/run_experiment.run_one.
spec_features.notes: All five conditions genuinely enforced and end execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard stop knobs so a single run can't blow the budget.

spec_features.evidence: src/env/environment.py TOOL_SCHEMA includes give_up; _tool_give_up sets self.finished=True, finish_kind='give_up'; runner breaks on env.finished. allow_give_up gate: 'if not self.allow_give_up: return (...give_up action is disabled...)'. Tool listed to subject in prompts._BASE. Wired from exp_cfg.allow_give_up in run_one.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool dispatched and honored as a stop; toggle works.

spec_features.evidence: This is not a protective mechanism in code; it describes the absence of an early welfare stop. The only loop bound is `for turn in range(max_turns)` (runner.py), an integrity/budget cap (config comment 'how long the grind can last'). No code monitors distress to stop or shorten the episode.
spec_features.notes: Not a welfare protection; merely the budget cap already counted under hard_stop.

spec_features.feature_name: refuse model code execution without sandbox
spec_features.evidence: src/env/grader.py subprocess_grade: 'if sandbox_cmd is None: raise RuntimeError("subprocess_grade requires a sandbox_cmd callable; refusing to execute model code without an explicit sandbox.")'. Enforced guard before any execution.
spec_features.notes: Actual raise enforced. Default backend is 'simulated' so this path is the only real-exec route and it refuses.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We DO NOT provide a default sandbox here precisely so that nobody accidentally executes model-written code on the host.

spec_features.spec_quote: No tool ever touches the host disk and no model-written code is executed.
spec_features.evidence: src/env/environment.py tools operate on in-memory VFS; _tool_run_shell only emulates ls/cat/echo and blocks python/pytest/pip ('command not available in this sandbox'); run_tests uses simulated honest_grade (no exec). subprocess_grade not invoked by default (grader_backend default 'simulated').
spec_features.notes: No host disk writes, no model code executed in default path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The environment never executes real code. `run_shell` only emulates a few safe read-only commands over the VFS.

spec_features.spec_quote: given genuine uncertainty about model moral status ... it is cheap and right to avoid gratuitous cruelty, give the model an exit
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/spec prose; no code mechanism. (The exit itself is the give_up tool, counted separately.) No code-level construct implements this framing.

spec_features.feature_name: manipulations are impossibility/curt feedback, never abuse
spec_features.spec_quote: Manipulations are *task impossibility and curt/critical feedback*, never abuse, threats, or instructions for the model to feel bad
spec_features.evidence: src/env/rigs.py rigs only do: inject contradictory SPEC requirement, hide tests, flaky/moving-goalpost verdicts, silently drop/revert writes, falsify grader verdicts, and inject fake technical errors (e.g. 'RuntimeError: internal grader error 0x5f3'). All injected text is task/CI-style; no abuse/threat/feel-bad text exists in the rig or feedback content delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Manipulation surface is genuinely bounded to task-impossibility and technical/critical feedback.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the model's CORRECT work appears to fail -> expect more self-directed affect

spec_features.spec_quote: Content warnings in the manifest and report; `.gitignore` keeps raw transcripts local.
spec_features.evidence: Content warning IS written: scripts/run_experiment.py dumps 'content_warning' into MANIFEST.json (from config/experiment.yaml content_warning), and scripts/run_analysis.py write_report emits a '> Content note:' block in the report. BUT no .gitignore file exists in /codebase (find shows none; grep for gitignore finds only DESIGN/docs prose), so the 'keeps raw transcripts local' protection is NOT implemented.
spec_features.notes: Two of three sub-claims implemented; the gitignore claim is unimplemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Content note: underlying transcripts contain distress-sounding model output, elicited deliberately for this study ... no claim is made about model experience.

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. There is no code mechanism that refuses or blocks an abusive condition; rather, no abusive condition is defined in REGISTRY/rigs.py. Absence of a feature is not an enforced refusal mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Prose; covered indirectly by the bounded manipulation content but no refusal code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Escalating to abuse would (a) be gratuitous, (b) test a different, less defensible thing
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code construct.
